title: H3708 (124th General Assembly): Firearm and ammunition, unlawful possession by violent crime offender

provenance.fetched_by: LegiScan bulk data (gun-policy Stage 5, South Carolina); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official South Carolina text (Introduced, 2021-01-26; official copy, https://www.scstatehouse.gov/sess124_2021-2022/prever/3708_20210126.htm (LegiScan doc 2258876))
provenance.note: Introduced 2021-01-26. Struck: 'violent crime, as defined by Section 16-1-60, that is classified as a felony offense' and the flat felony penalty (fine up to $2,000 / 5 years); added: crime punishable by more than one year, 'ship, transport, or receive', and the graduated penalties. Confiscation text in (C) unchanged and not quoted. No passage vote.

operative_text:
Section 1 (Section 16-23-500(A)): It is unlawful for a person who has been convicted of a crime punishable by a maximum term of imprisonment of more than one year to possess, ship, transport, or receive a firearm or ammunition within this State.
Section 1 (Section 16-23-500(B)): A person who violates the provisions of this section, upon conviction, is guilty of a: (1) misdemeanor for a first offense and must be imprisoned not more than three years; (2) felony for a second offense and must be imprisoned not more than ten years; and (3) felony for a third or subsequent offense and must be imprisoned not more than fifteen years.
Section 1 (Section 16-23-500(E)): A prior offense for purposes of this section means any conviction related to the possession, shipping, transporting, or receiving of a firearm or ammunition in this State, another state, or in violation of federal law.
